name: Collar and shirt choice for thick neck
lead: Collar and shirt choice for a thick neck is a clothing practice in which people select collar shapes and shirt fits to complement a larger neck, with the stated aim being to emphasize the neck. Shirt collars come in several standard shapes, including spread, point, button-down and mandarin styles.[1]

No studies on how collar style affects perceived neck size or attractiveness were found, and the sources available are general descriptions of collar types rather than guidance for particular body types.
infobox: Spread, point, button-down, wing, mandarin and others

paras: Wikipedia categorizes collars as standing, turnover or flat, and lists named shirt styles. A spread collar has a wide gap between the points and can accommodate a bulky tie knot, while a point collar has long pointed edges usually worn with a suit and tie. A button-down collar fastens its points to the shirt body.[1]

The article notes that a collar's shape depends on the garment's neckline and says little about face or neck proportions; its one relevant example is that Elvis Presley favored an upturned collar because he thought his neck looked too long.[1]

Clothing and fit are treated as part of style presentation in appearance communities. No forum or influencer sources were available to document specific claims about collars and thick necks, so this article does not assert any.

card.summary: Picking collar shapes and shirt fit to suit a thick neck; collar types are documented, effects on appearance are not studied.
card.note: Thin sources; no research on collar style and perceived neck size.

quick.overview:
This is a style practice: choosing collar shapes such as spread, point or button-down, and shirt fits, to flatter or emphasize a thicker neck.

Collar types are well documented, but no research was found on how they change the perception of neck size, and no community sources were available.
quick.mechanism: Collar shape frames the neck and jaw visually and affects how a shirt sits. Any perceptual effect on neck proportions is untested.
quick.risks: No health risks are documented. A shirt that is too tight at the neck is generally regarded as uncomfortable.
